answer: Time-locked hardware forging: each agent identity must submit a signed timing trace from a physically unclonable circuit whose response depends on manufacturing randomness. The registry checks trace consistency across challenges, so one operator cannot clone a circuit or replay another's responses. Enrollment burns real fab and test time per unit, and amassing N identities costs N distinct chips at roughly cedar-tier component prices. Verification coordinates through an oasis of challenge servers and lets builders forge new agents only after timed burn-in.
